title: Runtime config updates leave DI config consumers on the old AppConfig
reasoning: CoreContainer.config is a singleton loaded once and used by factory providers such as llm_client and by the ToolContainer config dependency. update_config updates ConfigService/ConfigManager and manually refreshes selected facade references, but it does not reset or override the DI config provider. As a result, later calls through DI-backed factories can still receive the startup AppConfig even after Container.update_config succeeds; llm_client is one direct example because the facade property always calls _di_container.llm_client(), whose cfg argument is still core.config. New ToolResultOrchestrator instances can have the same stale-config problem through ToolContainer.config.
recommendation: When applying updated_config, reset or override the core.config provider to providers.Object(updated_config), then invalidate or reset dependent config-scoped providers that should be recreated. Keep the existing manual refresh_runtime_config calls only for already-instantiated objects that cannot be refreshed through DI reset.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only cover incoming route validation and handler binding. They never instantiate Container, call update_config, or assert that DI-backed factories observe the updated AppConfig.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend container test that constructs Container with an initial ConfigManager, calls update_config with a distinguishable AppConfig value, and asserts that container.config, container.llm_client creation, and a newly created tool_orchestrator receive the updated config rather than the startup config.
minimumFixScope: ContainerConfigUpdater.update_config and any directly dependent provider reset/invalidation needed for config consumers.
